items.action: Follow-up: per-portal view webhook still inflates syndication stats on replay/retry — increment not gated on dedup (PR #2354) (Closes #2360)

Scheduler global-read RLS GUC leaks to pooled connection when set_global_read_context(conn,false) itself errors in fire_due_report_schedules (backend/servers/api-server/src/services/scheduler.rs:1416): the ? returns the connection with the session-level global-read GUC still set, so a later borrower without its own tenant context can read cross-org rows via the SELECT-only global-read policy leg (migration 00218). Clear the flag before the ? (mirror workflow_executor.rs guard.release() pattern) and add a regression test.

Scheduler metrics std::sync::Mutex<SchedulerMetrics> is locked with .lock().unwrap() on every tick of the indefinitely-running loop (backend/servers/api-server/src/services/scheduler.rs:168,314,377,497,549,832,858,878,1033,1163,1256,1323,1502,1511). A single panic while holding the lock poisons it and every subsequent tick panics, silently killing all scheduled work (announcements, votes, reminders, overdue transitions, report schedules). Replace with lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).
Follow-up: scheduler-RLS doc + test comments cite wrong migration number (00216 → should be 00218) (PR #2340) (Closes #2417)
Follow-up: cross-org /rag/migrate RLS test passes vacuously (runs as superuser) — switch to a NOBYPASSRLS role to actually guard the 00216 super-admin policy (PR #2335) (Closes #2418)
